summary: 日内瓦湖底快速堆积的沉积层，为六世纪文献记载的巨浪提供了实物证据。测年与模拟支持岩崩引发罗讷河三角洲沉积物垮塌、继而形成湖啸的解释，也提出了今日湖岸的风险。
logic: 古代巨浪记载缺少实证
湖底沉积层显示物质迅速堆积
模拟三角洲垮塌后的浪高与到达时间

paragraphs.brief: 在第六世纪，德国人叫弗兰克斯的古代古代古人格里戈里讲述了瑞士的一件大事，罗昂河泄漏到日内瓦湖。
sentences: In the sixth century Gregory of Tours, a chronicler* of the Germanic people known as the Franks, told of an extraordinary event in what is now Switzerland, where the Rhone River spills into Lake Geneva.
在第六世纪，德国人叫弗兰克斯的古代古代古人格里戈里讲述了瑞士的一件大事，罗昂河泄漏到日内瓦湖。
He wrote of a big rockfall in the year 563 AD in the vicinity of a place called Tauredunum.
他写了一篇关于563年在Tauredunum附近发生的大石头落下的报导。

The debris plunged into the river, and a great mass of water 'overwhelmed with a sudden and violent flood all that was on the banks as far as the city of Geneva,' more than 64 kilometres across the lake.
碎屑坠入河中，激起巨量的水。洪水“突然而猛烈地淹没了沿岸的一切”，一直冲到湖对岸 64 多公里外的日内瓦。
The Geneva bridge was demolished, and several people inside the city walls of Geneva were killed.
日内瓦桥被拆毁，日内瓦城墙内若干人被杀害。
Historians and scientists have long believed that Gregory and another chronicler, Marius of Avenches, who told a similar tale, were describing a tsunami that raced across the lake.
历史学家和科学家一直认为格雷戈里和另一个历史学家马略斯的阿文切斯讲述了一个类似的故事描述一场横跨湖的海啸
But there has not been any direct evidence of it until now.
但至今还没有任何直接的证据。

paragraphs.brief: 日内瓦大学的研究人员现在说，他们已经发现了这一证据，即湖中有大量沉积物。
sentences: Researchers at the University of Geneva now say they have found that evidence, in the form of a large deposit of sediment in the middle of the lake.
日内瓦大学的研究人员现在说，他们已经发现了这一证据，即湖中有大量沉积物。
In a study published in the journal Nature Geoscience, they also propose the sequence of events that caused the deadly surge.
在《自然地球科学》杂志上发表的一项研究中，他们还提出了造成致命性激增的事件的顺序。
The researchers think that large boulders crashed down onto soft sediments which had accumulated at the river mouth because of the slowing of the river's flow when it enters the lake.
研究人员认为，大块巨石坠落到软沉积物上，这些沉积物在河口积累，因为河水进入湖中时流动减缓。
These sediments formed an underwater delta that had several canyon-like channels.
这些沉积物形成一个水下三角洲，有几条类似峡谷的通道。
When the falling rocks hit the delta they destabilised the sediments and caused the canyons to collapse.
当坠落的岩石撞击三角洲时，它们破坏沉积物的稳定，并导致峡谷坍塌。
It was this collapse that created the tsunami.
海啸的起因就是这次崩溃
The sediments from this collapse would have been propelled towards the lake's centre.
这次塌陷的沉积物本来会被推向湖的中心

paragraphs.brief: 日内瓦大学地质学和古生物学系的讲师Guy Simpson说，厚厚的沉积物层与透镜形状相同，位于湖的最深处305米以上，大部分是偶然发现的。
sentences: Guy Simpson, a lecturer in the University of Geneva's Department of Geology and Paleontology, says the thick layer of sediment, which has the same curved shape as a lens, lies more than 305 metres down in the deepest part of the lake, and was found largely by chance.
日内瓦大学地质学和古生物学系的讲师Guy Simpson说，厚厚的沉积物层与透镜形状相同，位于湖的最深处305米以上，大部分是偶然发现的。

Katrina Kremer, a University of Geneva doctoral student and the study's lead author, had been conducting seismic soundings, searching for thin sediment layers that might be evidence of major floods that had taken place in pre-historic times, long before the event described by Gregory of Tours.
日内瓦大学博士生兼该研究的主要作者Katrina Kremer一直在进行地震探测，寻找可能是史前时期发生重大洪水的证据的薄沉积物层，远早于Gregory of Tours所描述的事件。
'But we came across this enormous deposit,' Simpson says.
辛普森说，我们碰见了这个巨大的存款
'We didn't know straight away that it was the deposit that caused the [sixth-century] tsunami.
我们不知道是存款导致了[六世纪]海啸
But it was a jumbled mess of sediment.
但它是一个乱七八糟的沉积物。
It was quite obvious that it was deposited rapidly.'
很明显它很快就沉没了

paragraphs.brief: 辛普森说，除了岩石瀑布之外，当时没有任何特别活动的记录。
sentences: The researchers then took samples of the sediments and used carbon-dating techniques on remains of leaves and other organic matter they found to determine when the deposit formed.
随后，研究人员采集沉积物样本，对其中找到的树叶残骸及其他有机物进行碳测年，以确定沉积层的形成年代。
This narrowed the range to a period between the late fourth century and the early seventh century.
这把范围缩小到四世纪末至七世纪初。
Other than the rockfall, there is no record of any special event during that period, Simpson says.
辛普森说，除了岩石瀑布之外，当时没有任何特别活动的记录。

paragraphs.brief: 研究人员估计，这个沉积层至少长 9.6 公里、宽 4.8 公里，平均厚约 5 米，所含物质超过 2.48 亿立方米。
sentences: The researchers estimated that the deposit, which is at least 9.6 kilometres long by 4.8 kilometres wide, and averages about five metres thick, contains more than 248 million cubic metres of material.
研究人员估计，这个沉积层至少长 9.6 公里、宽 4.8 公里，平均厚约 5 米，所含物质超过 2.48 亿立方米。

They ran multiple computer simulations showing that the collapse of that much sediment at the mouth of the Rhone would have caused a tsunami with an estimated height of 7.9 metres at Geneva - where it would have arrived in about 70 minutes.
他们进行了多次计算机模拟，显示Rhone河口大量沉积的塌陷可能造成海啸，估计日内瓦的高度为7.9米，大约70分钟后到达那里。
The rockfall itself may have been set off by a major earthquake, as some scientists have speculated.
正如一些科学家推测的那样，岩石本身可能因一场大地震而起落。

paragraphs.brief: 美国雷诺内华达大学荣誉地质学教授：“Richard Schweickert说，湖海啸虽然不同寻常，但并非未知。”
sentences: Lake tsunamis, although unusual, are not unknown, says Richard Schweickert, an Emeritus Professor of Geology at the University of Nevada in Reno, in the United States.
美国雷诺内华达大学荣誉地质学教授：“Richard Schweickert说，湖海啸虽然不同寻常，但并非未知。”
He cites evidence that the collapse of part of the shoreline of Lake Tahoe in northern California within the past 20,000 years caused a tsunami with wave heights of about 30 metres.
他引用证据表明，在过去20000年内，北加利福尼亚塔霍湖海岸线的一部分崩导致了大约30米的海。

There are two faults under the lake that could have caused an earthquake, he says and that the collapse of the Rhone delta sediments, as calculated by the Swiss researchers, 'would certainly be capable of moving a large amount of material into the lake.'
他说，湖下有两个断层可能导致地震，而且瑞士研究人员估计，Rhone 三角洲沉积物的崩溃“肯定能够将大量物质移入湖中。”
He suggests that the findings could be corroborated by careful mapping of the shoreline to look for unusual deposits or erosion left behind by the giant waves.
他建议，仔细绘制海岸线地图，寻找巨浪留下的不寻常矿床或侵蚀物，可以证实这些调查结果。

paragraphs.brief: 测试附近坡地的稳定性，并创建更详细的模型，说明海啸如何影响今天的日内瓦，这将更准确地评估湖边城市是否应该对此感到关切。
sentences: Simpson says the Rhone delta sediments might collapse again, perhaps from an earthquake or even their own weight.
辛普森说罗恩三角洲的沉积物可能会再次坍塌，也许是从地震中，甚至从它们自己的重量。

In the sixth century, Geneva was a small community, mostly behind walls on a hill, whereas today it is home to international organisations and about 200,000 people, many living in low-lying areas near the water.
6 世纪时，日内瓦还是一处小聚落，大多位于山丘上的城墙之内。如今，这里是许多国际组织的所在地，约有 20 万名居民，其中许多人住在近水的低洼地带。

Testing the stability of nearby slopes, and creating more detailed models of how a tsunami could affect Geneva today, would provide a more accurate assessment of whether or not this is something the lakeside city should be concerned about.
测试附近坡地的稳定性，并创建更详细的模型，说明海啸如何影响今天的日内瓦，这将更准确地评估湖边城市是否应该对此感到关切。

paragraphs.brief: 大多数海啸发生在海洋，是由地震引起的。
sentences: Most tsunamis occur in oceans and are generated by earthquakes.
大多数海啸发生在海洋，是由地震引起的。
However, the study is a reminder that even a landlocked nation like Switzerland is not immune to catastrophic waves.
然而，这项研究提醒人们，即使是像瑞士这样的内陆国家也不能免受灾难性的波浪的影响。

items.en: According to Gregory of Tours, the landslide which caused the flood happened near Tauredunum.
items.zh: 据Tours的Gregory说，造成洪水的滑坡发生在Tauredunum附近。
items.why: 图尔的格雷戈里把563年的山崩记在陶雷杜努姆附近，与题干地点相符。

items.en: The city of Geneva was undamaged by the tsunami that Gregory described.
items.zh: 日内瓦市没有因格雷戈里描述的海啸而受损。
items.why: 题干说“undamaged (毫发无损)”。但原文给出两类明确破坏: 桥被摧毁 + 城内有人死亡。这与“未受损” 直接矛盾，所以 FALSE。

items.en: The work of Marius of Avenches supported the idea that there was a tsunami.
items.zh: Avenches的Marius的工作支持发生海啸的想法。
items.why: 题干关键词 supported the idea (支持这一观点)。原文说 Marius told a similar tale (讲了相似故事),并且学者据此长期相信他们在描述海啸一-也就是把 Marius 的记载当作“支撑/佐 iE”. Att TRUE.

items.en: The rocks which fell into the delta were very hard and dense.
items.zh: 掉进三角洲的岩石非常坚硬和稠密
items.why: 文中只对“被砸的东西”给了性质: soft sediments (柔软沉积物)。对 boulders (巨石/岩块) 并没有说“hard and dense (坚硬上且致密)”.“boulder 常识上硬” 不能当成原文信息。题干两项性质 (hard + dense) 都未被明确陈述，所以NOT GIVEN。

items.en: Richard Schweickert has published studies on lake tsunamis that have occurred in several countries.
items.zh: 理查德·施韦克特发表了关于几个国家发生的湖泊海啸的研究报告。
items.why: 原文只说明他是教授、并且 cites evidence (引用证据) 举了 Lake Tahoe 的例子。没有说他发表研究 (published studies),也没有“several countries (多个国家)”。信息缺失，因此 NOT GIVEN。

items.en: The shoreline of Lake Tahoe has remained unchanged for 20,000 years.
items.zh: 塔霍湖的海岸线已经保持不变了20000年。
items.why: 题干说“remained unchanged (一直没变 )”,但原文说两万年内发生过湖岸雪塌 (collapse of part of the shoreline),这就意味着“有变化 "。与题干相反，故 FALSE。

items.en: Parts of the population of Geneva now live closer to the lake than was the case in the sixth century.
items.zh: 日内瓦部分人口现在生活在湖泊附近，比六世纪的情况更严重。
items.why: 对比结构 whereas (而如今) 很清晰: 过去“在山上城墙内”,现在“低洼靠水"。这就是“现在更靠近湖?。因此 TRUE。

items.en: Katrina Kremer was looking for indications of prehistoric ________ that had occurred before the sixth-century event.
items.zh: 卡特里娜·克雷默寻找的是史前________留下的迹象。这些事件早于公元6世纪的那次灾害。
items.why: 空前是“prehistoric (史前)”,原文对应名词是 major floods。按要求“一词”,填 floods.

items.en: Researchers extracted samples from the deposit and dated organic material such as ________
items.zh: 研究人员从沉积层中取样，并测定其中有机物的年代，例如________。
items.why: 题干“organic material such as…”对应原文举例 leaves,直接抄词即可。

items.en: Carbon-dating confirmed that the deposit was present in the lake by the beginning of the ________ century.
items.zh: 碳测年证实，到公元________世纪初，这片沉积层就已经存在于湖中了。
items.why: 流程图说“by the beginning of the _ century (到…世纪初)”。原文给出上限 early seventh century (七世纪初),因此填 seventh。

items.en: The volume of the deposit was then ________ by the scientists.
items.zh: 随后，科学家对沉积物的体积进行了________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“研究人员估计，这个沉积层至少长 9.6 公里、宽 4.8 公里，平均厚约 5 米，所含物质超过 2.48 亿立方米”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: The researchers established the approximate ________ and speed of the tsunami through extensive computer modelling.
items.zh: 研究人员通过大量计算机模拟，确定了海啸的大致________和传播速度。
items.why: 回到对应内容“他们进行了多次计算机模拟，显示Rhone河口大量沉积的塌陷可能造成海啸，估计日内瓦的高度为7.9米，大约70分钟后到达那里”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: A likely cause of the rockfall was a significant ________
items.zh: 这次山体崩塌的一个可能原因，是一场规模较大的________。
items.why: “significant”对应原文“major”。触发原因明确是 earthquake,填词即可。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词，可含数字。

pairs: 第 1 段 · 第 3 句
第 4 段 · 第 1 句
points: 文中只对“被砸的东西”给了性质: soft sediments (柔软沉积物)。对 boulders (巨石/岩块) 并没有说“hard and dense (坚硬上且致密)”.“boulder 常识上硬” 不能当成原文信息。题干两项性质 (hard + dense) 都未被明确陈述，所以NOT GIVEN。
“significant”对应原文“major”。触发原因明确是 earthquake,填词即可。
clauses: These sediments formed an underwater delta ….
“that had several canyon-like channels”修饰前面的 delta。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 delta，再把修饰信息接回主句。
“that it was the deposit that caused the [sixth-century] tsunami”补足 know 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 know 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: A chance finding by a Swiss research team explains an event that happened centuries ago around Lake Geneva
瑞士研究小组发现一个机会解释几个世纪前发生在日内瓦湖的一件事情
